## Welcome!

Hello and thank you for visiting my website! My name is Kelsey McGuire and I am a recent MSc graduate from the [Boreal-Arctic Biogeochemistry Lab](https://bab-lab.github.io/) under Dr. McKenzie Kuhn at the University of British Columbia. My MSc thesis sought to understand how vegetation along a Kaska lake shoreline alters methane (CH4) emission directly and indirectly, and you can access it [here](files/ubc_2026_november_mcguire_kelsey.pdf).

My professional interests include the restoration and protection of sensitive ecosystems, with wetlands having a special place in my environmental heart, alongside ensuring that environmental science is accessible, welcoming, and a safe space for people to enter and exist within. This involves ensuring that science is communicated in ways that everyone understands and can engage with.

I have been lucky to work with different research labs on a range of topics. If you want to learn more about the work I have done, please look at my [past research tab](/past-research.qmd)!

I would like to acknowledge that I am a visitor that lives and conducts research on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territories of the xʷməθkwəy̓əm [Musqueam](https://www.musqueam.bc.ca/), Skwxwú7mesh [Squamish](https://www.squamish.net/), and səlilwətaɬ/Selilwitulh [Tsleil-Waututh](https://twnation.ca/) nations. The research towards my current thesis has been conducted in partnership with the [Kaska Dena Kayeh](https://kaskadenacouncil.com/) peoples and I have been thankful to work on their land and to learn from their land guardians.
